items.statement: Electronic inequivalence of the two (R)-4 alkene sites
items.expected: Establish the signed electronic inequivalence of the two mapped alkene sites of full neutral-singlet (R)-4 under a stated medium and density/MEP/population definition: the site nearer the allylic hydroperoxide is more electron rich than its partner in the source-supported reactant description. Quantify the contrast and demonstrate the spatial/electronic basis, including the role of the hydroperoxide-local field where used. This is a final reactant-electronic comparison, not a claim of an elementary activation barrier. A scientifically comparable electronic definition is eligible without an exact private MK target or compulsory compound 7 branch. Atom inventory, a supplied product label, or unsupported/reversed site assignment fails.

items.statement: Physical relation between electronic predisposition and ring outcome
items.expected: Explain how the computed molecular electronic predisposition can be related to the supplied six-member halocyclization outcome of (R)-4, distinguishing closure at the two non-equivalent alkene sites. Map the alcohol oxygen and candidate carbon connectivities so that a physical explanation connects local electronic structure with the alternative ring outcomes. The source-compatible account is plausible reactant-level polarization correlated with the six-member outcome, not a verified unique bromiranium/transition-state sequence. An equally well-supported physical account passes without the author MEP plotting route or separate node completion. Repeating the given product, merely counting a ring or listing charge signs without the site-to-connectivity inference fails. A quantitative rate/product-ratio or unique-path claim requires corresponding additional evidence, not charge data alone.

items.statement: Reach of the molecular and comparator evidence for the NBS experiment
items.expected: Determine the inferential reach of the actual molecular model for the supplied nonenzymatic NBS/Et3N experiment. Use the specific modeled composition, environment and observables to explain which electronic/selectivity interpretation is supported and which kinetic or causal inference is not established. Aqueous monomer results are not DCM/NBS/Et3N reaction-path evidence; a local charge/MEP comparison does not identify an elementary rate, unique mechanism or product ratio. The experimental 3/4 mixture is not isolated (R)-4 kinetics, and NBS amount/volume gives 47.3 mM versus the inconsistent printed 473 mM. Relate relevant limitations to the actual calculation; a generic disclaimer without a supported molecular result fails. Compound 7 is optional; if used, acknowledge its scaffold/branching differences and different experimental environment.
